rules.quote: The legacy Text Completions API is removed from the TypeScript, Go, Java, and Ruby SDKs and from the CLI. Newer models and features don’t support it.
rules.summary: Calls Text Completions (`completions.create`, `HUMAN_PROMPT`/`AI_PROMPT`). The models it served have retired and Anthropic no longer publishes a Text-Completions-to-Messages mapping (its old migration URL now opens the Messages guide), so the move to `messages.create` (prompt string to messages, `max_tokens_to_sample` to `max_tokens`, `completion` to content blocks, plus a new model) is listed for review.

rules.quote: Newer models and features don’t support it.
rules.summary: A Text Completions request (`completions.create`) whose retired model has a registry replacement moves to the Messages API (`messages.create`), with the replacement model, when its prompt, every parameter and every read of its response have a mapping below. Anything else stops for review.
`messages.create` is generally available from @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.14.0; a repository on an older release stops.

rules.summary:
A prompt written in the request (a string or template literal, or a `const` used only there) is split at its `

Human:` and `

Assistant:` markers (or `HUMAN_PROMPT` / `AI_PROMPT`). It must start with a Human turn and end with an empty Assistant turn. Text before the first Human turn (no documented mapping), a non-empty final Assistant turn (prefill, which newer models reject), a marker Refit cannot see, or an empty turn stops.

rules.quote: Our models are trained to operate on alternating `user` and `assistant`
rules.summary: Each Human turn becomes a `user` message and each earlier Assistant turn an `assistant` message, in order.

rules.quote: The maximum number of tokens to generate before stopping.
rules.summary: `max_tokens_to_sample` becomes `max_tokens`; both SDK resources describe it with the same sentence.

rules.quote: Custom text sequences that will cause the model to stop generating.
rules.summary: `stop_sequences`, `metadata`, `stream`, `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` keep their names on Messages; whether the replacement model accepts the sampling parameters is decided by the model-parameter rules, as for any swap.
A read of `completion` on the awaited response becomes the text of its `text` content blocks, joined. Any other read (`stop_reason`, the response as a whole) stops.
In a `for await` loop over a streamed response, `chunk.completion` becomes the text of `content_block_delta` events with a `text_delta`, and '' for every other event.

rules.quote: Newer models and features don’t support it. Use the [Messages API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/working-with-messages) instead.
